subject: Request: Residency scope for PII-derived embeddings & cross-region telemetry exception
message_1:
From: Sara Lim <sara@helixhealth.com>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
Date: 2027-03-16 08:12:00 +01:00
Subject: Residency question: PII-derived embeddings and telemetry

Hi Diego,

Thanks for the demo last week — the platform looks promising. Before we proceed with the pilot, Legal and Security asked for a clear statement on two items so we can sign the DPA addendum:

1) Residency scope for PII-derived embeddings: we will be supplying patient identifiers and generating embeddings for enrichment. We need confirmation that embeddings (and any derived vectors) created from EU patient data will be stored and served only from EU-bound infrastructure (including the vector DB and any cache layers). Does Redwood treat derived embeddings as "customer data" under the DPA or as telemetry/derived metrics?

2) Cross-region telemetry: your team mentioned transient analytics telemetries for performance tuning (e.g., sample traces, token-level latency aggregates). Please confirm whether any traces or telemetry that include signal from EU requests could leave the EU region transiently, and if so, what safeguards (aggregation window, pseudonymization, TTL) apply.

We also need a subprocessor roster for legal review. Can you share a draft DPA addendum and the active subprocessor roster? Procurement is looped: procurement@helixhealth.com.

Appreciate a short written response and we can follow with a 30-minute call if helpful.

Thanks,
Sara Lim
Lead, Security Risk - Helix Health

---
Attachment: none
message_2:
From: diego_fernandez@redwood.com
To: Sara Lim <sara@helixhealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2027-03-16 09:25:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Residency question: PII-derived embeddings and telemetry

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear asks. Quick answers up front, then attachments and next steps.

Short answers:
- Embeddings and derived vectors are treated as customer data and can be pinned to a region per contract (we support model + storage affinity). For EU-pinned workloads, vectors, cache entries, and the vector DB instance will be provisioned within the EU region.
- Telemetry (sampling traces, aggregated latency histograms) is collected for platform monitoring. For EU-pinned customers we have two modes: (a) telemetry retained and processed in EU only, or (b) telemetry aggregated/pseudonymized at edge and allowed to cross-region for global analytics. We recommend (a) for regulated PII workloads.

I attached a draft DPA addendum (v2) that includes explicit language treating embeddings as "customer content" and a subprocessor roster stub. Please review.

Operational notes:
- Vector DB replication: by default we do not replicate the customer’s vector DB outside the pinned region. Cross-region replication is opt-in and requires written approval.
- Caching: we can disable cross-region prefix caching; local KV caches are per-region.
- KMS: we support customer-managed KMS keys in EU (bring-your-own-key). If you supply a key stored in an EU KMS, no key material leaves region.

Propose a 30-min call tomorrow 10:00 CET to walk through wording and signing flow.

Regards,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

---
Attachments: DPA_addendum_draft_v2.pdf (draft), subprocessor_roster_stub.csv (list, redacted)

message_4:
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: Sara Lim <sara@helixhealth.com>
Cc: diego_fernandez@redwood.com, grace_oconnor@redwood.com
Date: 2027-03-17 09:03:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Residency question: PII-derived embeddings and telemetry

Hi Sara — Jonas from infra here, short technical clarifications: 

1) Encryption & BYOK: if you use Redwood's BYOK flow with an EU KMS (Azure Key Vault / GCP KMS / AWS KMS in eu-west region), all envelope key operations (wrap/unwrap) occur within the EU. The platform will not export unwrapped key material. The vector DB is envelope-encrypted, and we support customer-managed keys for the DB and for object stores that hold snapshots.

2) Replication/caching: we will not configure cross-region replication for Helix's EU-pinned vector DB unless you explicitly approve it. Caches are region-local by default; we can disable prefix caching across regions.

3) Telemetry specifics (mode b, if you opt-in):
   - Aggregation window: 1 minute rollups for latency histograms, 24-hour TTL for aggregated records that leave the EU for global analytics.
   - Redaction: token-level traces are hashed and truncated; raw prompt text and PII fields are removed prior to export.
   - Sampling: <0.1% request sampling for full traces; only aggregated metrics leave by default.

4) Deletion/retention: embeddings stored in the vector DB follow the same delete APIs as other customer objects. When you request deletion we enqueue an immediate delete and background scrubbing; typical full purge across backups/snapshots completes within 72 hours (we document this in the DPA addendum).

Link to our residency runbook and telemetry playbook: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-helix-residency-playbook

Happy to join the call tomorrow to review the technical appendix.

—Jonas
Principal Engineer, Platform Infra
